_comment: Saved character configuration for rust-scavenger. Modeled on character-bounds.json (the courier's) — see that file for the long-form rationale on every field below; this copy states only what differs for a ground patroller. THE SCALE LIVES HERE ON PURPOSE (vault A5): a global constant derived from a single regenerable frame means regenerating that frame silently rescales every other animation and moves every measured bound. `npm run assets:build` READS this and never computes it; `node tools/gen/build-assets.mjs rust-scavenger <action> --derive-scale` prints a new one for a human to paste in deliberately.
_scale: Source pixels to game pixels. DERIVED 2026-08-11 (session 6) from `rust-scavenger-walk-r3.mp4` — 240 / 428 = 0.56074766. Pasted by hand from `node tools/gen/build-assets.mjs rust-scavenger walk --derive-scale`, which PRINTS it and never writes it (vault A5: the build reads this number and never computes it). ⚠️ MEASURED FROM A GAIT, NOT A NEUTRAL POSE, and that is not a shortcut — the scavenger patrols continuously and has NO `idle`, deliberately, because a standing pose is a state the sim cannot enter. The twelve walk frames span a mean height of 428 source px with a frame-to-frame spread of 18 px, **4.2%** — against the sentry's 0.3% and the courier's 0.8%. That spread IS the size-pop this scale exists to hold still, and it is larger here because a striding figure genuinely changes height within its cycle; averaging over a full closed cycle (the clip yields exactly 2.0 cycles) is what makes the mean meaningful rather than arbitrary. Re-deriving is mandatory if the walk clip is ever re-shot, and `chase`/`death` must be packed against whatever value stands here, never the reverse. Shares the provenance limitation recorded for the courier and the sentry (Codex C5, docs/qa/phase-05-combat.md limitation 7): the source is a regenerable sheet, not the locked anchor — the anchor cannot supply it, being 3690 square against a 960 square clip.
_renderHeightPx: SCAVENGER_BOX.h (40 sim px, src/sim/enemyPlacement.ts) x RENDER_SCALE (6, src/game/constants.ts) = 240 px = 2.5 tiles. Between the sentry's 192 px and the courier's 288 px on purpose — three distinct silhouette heights (src/sim/enemyPlacement.ts's own header on SENTRY_BOX/SCAVENGER_BOX).
_frame: The ONE global cell size (decision M3), 3 x 4 tiles at TILE_SIZE 96 — same as the courier's and the sentry's, NOT shrunk for a smaller subject.
_baseline: Same per-SHEET contact-frame rule as the courier's file (see character-bounds.json's `_baseline` note).

collisionBox._source: SCAVENGER_BOX x RENDER_SCALE (src/sim/enemyPlacement.ts:94). The ART is drawn narrower than this at the anchor, which is the safe direction, same as the courier's.

_stride: NOT YET MEASURED — no packable clip exists for walk or chase (same blocker as `_scale` above). Needed once a clip lands: `walk`/`chase` are the 'measured' rows in src/render/animTiming.ts's enemyAnimTimings, so their catalog fps is derived from `strideTicks(stride, SCAVENGER.patrolSpeed|chaseSpeed)` the same way the courier's walk/run are, never authored.
_animations: ['walk','chase','death'] — must equal configFor('rust-scavenger').actions in tools/gen/slugConfig.mjs and ANIMS_BY_SLUG['rust-scavenger'] in src/render/enemyView.ts. There is no `idle`: the scavenger patrols continuously (src/render/enemyView.ts's `scavengerAnim`), so a standing pose is never reached and a sheet for it would be money spent on a state the sim cannot enter. `verticalAnchor` is 'feet' for all three: the scavenger never leaves the ground, same reasoning as the sentry's file.
_activeFrames: Empty for every animation. The scavenger has no attack state — its BODY is the hazard (contact damage, no swing, src/render/enemyView.ts's header) — so there is no strike window to align a per-frame hitbox against for this slug.
